chunks: It is narrated that mut'ah (exit from Ihram) was revealed to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) at Marwah after completing the Sa'y.

He said: 'O people, this is Jibril'—and he gestured with his hand behind him—'commanding me to order those who have not brought sacrificial animals to exit Ihram. If I had known beforehand what I know now, I would have done as I am commanding you. However, I have brought the sacrificial animals, and it is not permissible for the one bringing the sacrificial animals to exit Ihram until the sacrificial animals reach their place.'

Then Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum Al-Kinani stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you have taught us our religion as if we were created today. Is what you have commanded us specific to this year, or is it forever?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No, rather it is for eternity.'

A man stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we will return from Hajj with our heads dripping (with water from purification after relations)?' The Prophet replied: 'You will never believe in this, ever.'

When Imam Ali (peace be upon him) was in Yemen, upon his return, he found that Fatima (peace be upon her) had exited Ihram. Imam (as) approached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) seeking clarification and expressing concern about Fatima's (peace be upon her) actions. The Prophet said to him: 'I am the one who commanded the people to do so. And with what intention did you enter Ihram, O Ali (as)?'

Imam Ali (as) replied: 'With the same intention as the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).' The Prophet then said: 'Remain in Ihram like me, for you are my partner in the sacrificial offering.'

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) had brought one hundred camels for sacrifice. He allocated thirty-four of them to Imam Ali (as) and sixty-six for himself. He sacrificed them all with his own hand.
From each camel, he took a portion of meat, cooked it in a pot, and both of them ate from it and drank its broth. The Prophet said: 'We have now eaten from them all together.'
They did not give the hides, saddles, or ornaments of the camels to the butchers but instead donated them as charity.

key_terms.إِهْلَالٌ: Ihram: The sacred state of consecration entered by pilgrims.
key_terms.السَّعْيُ: Sa'y: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwah.
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: Mut'ah: Exiting the state of Ihram for Umrah while remaining in the state of Hajj, or exiting Ihram completely while staying in the Haram area.
key_terms.الْهَدْيُ: Hady: The sacrificial animal(s) brought by the pilgrim.
key_terms.جَذْوَةٌ: Jadhwah: A portion or piece of meat.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Mut'ah in Hajj and how did Imam Ali's Ihram status relate to the Prophet's?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* clarifies the ruling of *Hajj al-Tamattu'* by distinguishing between pilgrims who brought sacrificial animals (*had'y*) and those who did not, establishing the Prophet's authority to command the latter to exit Ihram while the former must remain until their sacrifice is completed. It further illustrates the unique spiritual and ritual bond between the Prophet and Imam Ali, who, despite being in Yemen, aligned his Ihram status with the Prophet's, resulting in a shared sacrifice of one hundred camels that they consumed together, emphasizing their unity in religious practice.
